prompt: Paint a close still life at an evening theater box-office counter in opaque gouache. One small tangerine-orange paper admission ticket lies flat on the palm of a white cotton glove resting on the counter. It should be the first thing the eye finds: give its punched paper silhouette a crisp edge and reserve the one vivid warm note for it. Indigo-violet theater light falls across the glove, giving the folds cool reflected color while the softly pale ridges, seam and weave clearly read as white cloth. Suggest the ticket window behind in subdued broad shapes. Use matte, overlapping opaque brushstrokes on paper.

Paint a teahouse windowsill at sunset in transparent watercolor. A single small red raspberry sits on a shallow pale celadon-glazed ceramic plate. Let the tiny fruit be the immediate point of attention, its clear red and sharply gathered drupelets surrounded by quiet pale blue-green glaze. Amber sunset light grazes the plate at the window side; allow the pale turquoise local color to show across the curved body and shadow. Use transparent overlapping washes, reserved paper highlights and softened edges in the receding window and teahouse shapes. Keep the evening light soft so it supports the fruit.

Draw a carpenter's workbench under a blue work lamp entirely in colored pencil. Show a black leather tool pouch on the bench, with one small yellow carpenter's pencil tucked into the pocket, its exposed flattened shaft clearly emerging past the leather lip. Catch the eye first with this little flash of bright yellow and its distinct edge. Keep the leather convincingly black: dark body, subdued blue reflections skimming the bent rim, creases and grain. Describe the workbench and pool of cool light with quieter layered pencil strokes, crosshatching and visible paper tooth.
